title: Regularization of smooth-generic nodal families
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$, residue field $k$, and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $X\to S$ be projective [def-kun-projective], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with nonempty nodal geometric fibres. Assume $X_K$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. There is a finite sequence $T=X_m\to\cdots\to X_0=X$ in which every arrow is the blowup of a reduced closed point where the total scheme $X_j$ is not regular [def-nagata-global-blowup, def-weil-regular-scheme]. Every $X_j\to S$ remains projective, flat and finitely presented with nodal geometric fibres, and $T$ is regular. All centres lie in the special fibre. The composite is an isomorphism on the generic fibre and on the relative smooth locus of $X$. Each arrow is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] with nonempty geometrically connected fibres. A nodal geometric fibre here is reduced of pure dimension one, and each nonsmooth closed point has completed local ring $\Omega[[x,y]]/(xy)$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. The intermediate geometric fibres need not be connected. The regular scheme $T$ is a finite disjoint union of integral regular surfaces of dimension two. Local rings at generic points of its special-fibre components are DVRs.

source.place: Tag 0CDE (lemma-blowup-at-worst-nodal), with charts in Tag 0CDC (example-blowup). Projectivity and geometrically connected exceptional fibres are consequences of the displayed blowup charts; disconnected geometric fibres are permitted.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-nodal-trait-finite-singular-charts] to $X/S$. Its hypotheses hold without connectedness: $X$ is Noetherian and its nonregular points form a finite set $E$ of closed special-fibre points. Each $x\in E$ has a chosen pointed model of exponent $n_x\geq2$; no intrinsic or choice-independent exponent is needed.

For a selected $x$ with chosen exponent $n$, induct on $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$. By [lem-sfb-nodal-point-blowup-local-descent] one reduced-point blowup preserves the nodal flat locally finitely presented family, is unchanged away from $x$, and removes all nonregular points above $x$ if $n=2,3$. For $n\geq4$ there is exactly one nonregular descendant, with pointed model exponent $n-2$; apply the induction hypothesis, since $\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor=\lfloor n/2\rfloor-1$. At every blowup [lem-sfb-nodal-point-blowup-projective-fibres] applies: the current scheme is Noetherian and projective, the chosen pointed model supplies its local hypothesis, and local descent supplies flatness and local finite presentation. It retains projectivity, finite presentation and nonempty family fibres, and gives proper arrows with nonempty geometrically connected fibres. Thus at most $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ arrows remove $x$ without altering the other points of $E$. Induct now on $|E|$: for $E=\varnothing$ use the identity tower; otherwise this finite tower reduces $|E|$ by one. The concatenated finite tower ends in a regular $T$.

source.place: Tag 0CDE (lemma-blowup-at-worst-nodal), point-blowup comparison and nested finite induction, with Tag 0CDC (example-blowup).

proof.text: Every centre is special by step 1, reapplied to each stage. Each arrow is an isomorphism off its centre by [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement], hence on the generic fibre. Over the original relative smooth locus the composite stays an isomorphism: this locus is regular by [lem-sfb-nodal-trait-finite-singular-charts]; if its current inverse image is isomorphic to it, it is regular and contains no next nonregular centre, so the next complement isomorphism preserves this assertion. This proves both isomorphism clauses.

source.place: Tag 0CDE (lemma-blowup-at-worst-nodal), singular centres and the complement isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-regular-trait-curve-surface-components] to $T/S$. It is H-projective by step 2 (by hypothesis if the tower is empty), hence proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], and it is flat, Noetherian and regular by step 2; its reduced special fibre follows from nodality. The local dimension upper bound two and equality two at closed special points follow by applying [lem-sfb-nodal-trait-finite-singular-charts] to this last family, whose generic fibre stayed smooth. The cited component theorem gives the required finite disjoint union of integral regular surfaces and DVR stalks at all special-component generic points.
